meta.title: Leema Engineering Web Design Case Study — GCC Industrial Supplier | Teknoppy
meta.description: How Teknoppy restructured leemaeng.com for a Sharjah-based pipes, fittings, and flanges supplier serving the wider GCC — a clear pillar and location structure for a 50-year industrial brand.

paragraphs.text: Leema Engineering Works (LEW) is an ISO 9001-2015 certified pipes, fittings, and flanges supplier based in Sharjah, UAE, with over 50 years of legacy serving the Oil & Gas, Power, Steel, Marine, Water Treatment, Food, and Mining sectors across Sharjah, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and the wider GCC. Teknoppy's goal was to restructure the site around a clear pillar and location framework that could represent the full breadth of LEW's products, services, and GCC-wide reach, without pages competing against each other for the same search terms.

rows.label: Key Services
rows.value: Web Design, Website Structure & Information Architecture, SEO

items.title: Repetitive, keyword-stuffed content
items.text: Phrases like "Sharjah, Dubai and UAE" were repeated throughout nearly every section of the site instead of being supported by structured, location-specific pages, diluting rather than strengthening local relevance.

items.title: Products, services, and industries loosely bundled
items.text: Pipes, fittings, flanges, valves, and accessories sat under a handful of broad sections rather than a clear, expandable pillar structure.

items.title: Limited GCC coverage
items.text: Only isolated pages existed for Bahrain and Qatar, with no consistent structure extending coverage to the wider GCC market LEW actually serves.

items.title: An eight-pillar content structure (directly answers Problem 1 & 2)
items.text: A full 66-page restructure organizes LEW's products, services, and industries into eight distinct topical pillars, replacing scattered, repetitive sections with a clear, expandable framework.

items.title: 15 location pages across the GCC (directly answers Problem 3)
items.text: Dedicated location pages, including Bahrain, extend structured coverage across the wider GCC market instead of leaving it to a couple of isolated pages.

items.title: Cannibalization-aware structure
items.text: Pillars and location pages are built to stay distinct from one another, so overlapping products and regions don't end up competing for the same search terms.

paragraphs.text: Discovery, pillar mapping, and page-by-page build details specific to this project — timeline and key decisions — should be pulled from the project intake and added here once confirmed.

items.q: What was the main goal of the Leema Engineering website project?
items.a: To restructure a 50-year industrial supplier's site around a clear pillar and location framework that represents its full product range and GCC-wide reach without pages competing against each other.
Pipes, pipe fittings, flanges, valves, and industrial accessories for the Oil & Gas, Power, Steel, Marine, Water Treatment, Food, and Mining sectors.

items.q: Which locations does the new structure cover?
items.a: 15 location pages across the GCC, including Bahrain, alongside LEW's core Sharjah, Dubai, and Abu Dhabi coverage.

items.q: Did the project affect Leema Engineering's existing rankings?
items.a: The restructure was scoped to avoid keyword cannibalization across LEW's product, service, and location pages — no overlapping targets were introduced.
